[![Image 14](http://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/Seymour_sq%2C_Blenheim.JPG/250px-Seymour_sq%2C_Blenheim.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Seymour_sq,_Blenheim.JPG)

Seymour Sq, Blenheim in early spring 2012

[Omaka Aerodrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omaka_Aerodrome "Omaka Aerodrome"), south of the town centre, is the setting for the two-yearly [Classic Fighters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classic_Fighters "Classic Fighters") Marlborough airshow. With a large emphasis on aircraft of World War One, it has been held since 2001.

Seymour Square and Pollard Park are two of the town centres main attractions for walks and general tourism. Seymour Square is an open public area in the centre, containing the War Memorial and Clock Tower, unveiled in 1928, classified as a "Category I" ("places of 'special or outstanding historical or cultural heritage significance or value'") historic place by [Heritage New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heritage_New_Zealand "Heritage New Zealand").[[28]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-28) The Square was named after Henry Seymour.[[29]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-29) Pollard Park is a large public park including children's play areas, native shrubbery, rose gardens, a landscaped waterway, and is home to the Blenheim Golf Club and its 9-hole course, the Marlborough Tennis club and its courts, and Blenheim Croquet Club. They are dry and arid ranges which have previously been the site of severe grass fires.

The [GCSB Waihopai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GCSB_Waihopai "GCSB Waihopai") communications monitoring facility, part of the [ECHELON](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECHELON "ECHELON") network, is near Blenheim.

## Transport

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blenheim,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Transport")]

### Air

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blenheim,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Air")]

[Woodbourne Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodbourne_Airport "Woodbourne Airport") is a [domestic airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_airport "Domestic airport") and an [RNZAF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_New_Zealand_Air_Force "Royal New Zealand Air Force") operational base. There are direct flights from [Auckland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland "Auckland") and [Wellington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellington "Wellington") with [Air New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_New_Zealand "Air New Zealand") and from [Wellington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellington "Wellington"), [Christchurch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christchurch "Christchurch"), and [Paraparaumu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraparaumu "Paraparaumu") with [Sounds Air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sounds_Air "Sounds Air").[[30]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-30)

[Omaka Aerodrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omaka_Aerodrome "Omaka Aerodrome"), to the south of the town centre, is used solely by private and vintage aircraft. The [Classic Fighters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classic_Fighters "Classic Fighters") airshow (based mainly on World War I and II aircraft) is held biennially at Easter.

### Road

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blenheim,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Road")]

[State Highway 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1 "New Zealand State Highway 1") runs through Blenheim and [State Highway 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Highway_6_(New_Zealand) "State Highway 6 (New Zealand)") terminates at the junction of the two state highways. Blenheim is notable for a town of its size in that it does not have [traffic lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traffic_light "Traffic light") at any intersection.[[31]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-31) Instead, [roundabouts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roundabout "Roundabout") speed arterial traffic flow. Since the installation of roundabouts traffic volumes have quickly increased and upgrading options are being considered, e.g. traffic lights, longer two-lane approaches and even a bypass.[[32]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-32)

### Rail

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blenheim,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Rail")]

Blenheim is on the [Main North Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_North_Line,_New_Zealand "Main North Line, New Zealand"), the northern part of the unofficially-named [South Island Main Trunk Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Island_Main_Trunk_Railway "South Island Main Trunk Railway"). The [Coastal Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coastal_Pacific "Coastal Pacific"), a long-distance passenger train between Picton and Christchurch, stops at [Blenheim railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim_railway_station "Blenheim railway station").[[33]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-33) The 1906 station has been listed [NZHPT Category II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heritage_New_Zealand#The_Register "Heritage New Zealand") since 1982.[[34]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-34) It is a [standard Vintage station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Troup_(architect)#Standard_Station_designs "George Troup (architect)"), with Tudor half-timbering and tile.[[35]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-35)

A major rail freight facility is north of Blenheim at [Spring Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_Creek,_New_Zealand "Spring Creek, New Zealand").

The narrow-gauge [Blenheim Riverside Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim_Riverside_Railway "Blenheim Riverside Railway") runs through the town.

## Infrastructure and services

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blenheim,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Infrastructure and services")]

### Electricity

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blenheim,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Electricity")]

The Marlborough Electric Power Board (MEPB) was formed in October 1923 and established the Blenheim's first public supply in April 1927, following the commissioning of the Waihopai hydroelectric power station 40 km southwest of Blenheim. Two diesel generators were commissioned at Springlands in 1930 and 1937 to supplement the supply from Waihopai. The town was connected to [Cobb Power Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cobb_Power_Station "Cobb Power Station") in 1945,[[36]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-36) which in turn was connected to the rest of the South Island grid in 1956. The diesel generators were relegated to standby duty, last generated power on 22 July 1992, and were decommissioned in 2003. The Energy Companies Act 1992 saw the MEPB corporatised and renamed Marlborough Electric. The 1998 electricity sector reforms required electricity companies to separate their lines and supply businesses. Marlborough Electric sold its generation and retailing business to [Trustpower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trustpower "Trustpower"), with the remaining lines business renamed [Marlborough Lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlborough_Lines_Limited "Marlborough Lines Limited").[[37]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-37)

Today, Marlborough Lines owns and operates the electricity distribution network servicing the town, with electricity fed from [Transpower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transpower_New_Zealand_Limited "Transpower New Zealand Limited")'s national grid at its Blenheim substation in Springlands.

### Water supply and sanitation

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blenheim,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Water supply and sanitation")]

Blenheim's water supply is drawn from the Wairau aquifer via nine bores and is treated at two plants in Middle Renwick Road and Bomford Street.[[38]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-38)

## Education

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blenheim,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Education")]

The first school opened in 1859. By 1875 there were three classes: Blenheim Upper Boys', Blenheim Lower Boys', and Blenheim Girls' and Infants'. Blenheim High School was formed within the school in 1879.[[39]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-39)

Catholic schools for boys and girls were established in 1872, replaced by St Mary's Boys' School in 1886. In 1929 St Mary's was rebuilt after a fire.[[40]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-40)

Marlborough High School, a coeducational secondary school, was founded in Blenheim in 1900. In 1919 it changed its name to Marlborough College. The intermediate section was split to form Bohally Intermediate in 1956. The college was split into separate boys' and girls' schools in 1963, with Marlborough Boys' College (MBC) retaining the existing site and Marlborough Girls' College (MGC) moving to a new site.[[41]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-41) An intention to relocate both Marlborough Boys' College and Marlborough Girls' College on the site currently occupied by MGC and Bohally Intermediate was announced in 2019, with Bohally Intermediate relocating to the current MBC site on Stephenson Street.[[42]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-42) The relocation plan was scrapped in 2024.[[43]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-43)

There are currently 11 schools in the Blenheim urban area: [[44]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-NZ_school_roll_data-44)

*   **Blenheim School** is a state contributing primary (Year 1–6) primary school. It has a roll of approximately 144.
*   **Bohally Intermediate** is a state intermediate (Year 7–8) school opened in 1957 following a split from Marlborough College. It has a roll of approximately 532.
*   **[Marlborough Boys' College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlborough_Boys'_College "Marlborough Boys' College")** is a state boys' secondary (Year 9–13) school. It opened in 1963 following the split of Marlborough College into separate boys' and girls schools, and has a roll of approximately 1,024.
*   **[Marlborough Girls' College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlborough_Girls'_College "Marlborough Girls' College")** is a state girls' secondary (Year 9–13) school. It opened in 1963 following the split of Marlborough College into separate boys' and girls school, and has a roll of approximately 960.
*   **Mayfield School** is a state contributing primary (Year 1–6) school in [Mayfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayfield,_Blenheim "Mayfield, Blenheim"). It has a roll of approximately 97.
*   **Redwoodtown School** is a state full primary (Year 1–8) school in [Redwoodtown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redwoodtown "Redwoodtown"). It has a roll of approximately 308.
*   **Richmond View School** is a state-integrated Christian composite (Year 1–13) school in Redwoodtown. It has a roll of approximately 330.
*   **Springlands School** is a state contributing primary (Year 1–6) school in [Springlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springlands "Springlands"). It has a roll of approximately 350.
*   **St Mary's School** is a state-integrated Catholic full primary (Years 1–8) school. It has a roll of approximately 171.
*   **Whitney Street School** is a state contributing primary (Year 1–6) primary school. It has a roll of approximately 369.
*   **Witherlea School** is a state contributing primary (Year 1–6) primary school in [Witherlea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Witherlea "Witherlea"). It has a roll of approximately 388.

Other primary schools are in the surrounding localities of [Renwick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renwick,_New_Zealand "Renwick, New Zealand"), [Fairhall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairhall "Fairhall"), [Grovetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grovetown,_New_Zealand "Grovetown, New Zealand"), [Rapaura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapaura "Rapaura") and [Riverlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverlands "Riverlands").

The [Nelson Marlborough Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Marlborough_Institute_of_Technology "Nelson Marlborough Institute of Technology") has a campus in Blenheim.[[45]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim,_New_Zealand#cite_note-45)

## Media

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blenheim,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Media")]

### Print

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blenheim,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Print")]

Blenheim is served by a variety of print publications. The major daily newspaper serving the area is _[The Marlborough Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Marlborough\_Express "The Marlborough Express")_ published by Fairfax NZ, with its headquarters in Blenheim. _The Saturday Express_ and _Midweek_ are community newspapers published by the same company and distributed throughout Marlborough. _The Blenheim Sun_ is a twice-weekly free newspaper distributed each Wednesday and Friday while the locally owned _Marlborough Weekly_ is published every Tuesday and delivered to every home in the region.

### Radio

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Blenheim,_New_Zealand&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Radio")]

Blenheim is [served by 22 FM radio stations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_radio_stations_in_Marlborough "List of radio stations in Marlborough"). The town can also receive AM and FM radio stations from Wellington, due to the straight line-of-sight across Cook Strait and the high power of the transmitters.

**State Highway 1** (**SH 1**) is the longest and most significant road in the [New Zealand road network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_state_highway_network "New Zealand state highway network"), running the length of both main islands. It appears on road maps as SH 1 and on road signs as a white number 1 on a red shield, but it has the official designations SH 1N in the [North Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Island "North Island") and SH 1S in the [South Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Island "South Island").

SH 1 is 2,006 kilometres (1,246 mi) long, 1,074 km (667 mi) in the North Island[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-1) and 932 km (579 mi) in the South Island.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-2) Since 2010 new roads have reduced the length from 2,033 km (1,263 mi).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-3) For the majority of its length it is a two-lane [single carriageway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_carriageway "Single carriageway"), with [at-grade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/At-grade_intersection "At-grade intersection") intersections and property accesses, in both rural and urban areas. These sections have some passing lanes. Around 315 km (196 mi) of SH 1 is of motorway or expressway standard as of August 2022[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_Highway_1_(New_Zealand)&action=edit): 281 km (175 mi) in the North Island and 34 km (21 mi) in the South Island.[_[needs update](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers#Chronological\_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_]

### North Island (SH 1N)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_Highway_1_(New_Zealand)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: North Island (SH 1N)")]

SH 1 starts at [Cape Reinga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Reinga "Cape Reinga"), at the northwestern tip of the [Aupōuri Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aup%C5%8Duri_Peninsula "Aupōuri Peninsula"), and since April 2010 has been [sealed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sealed_road "Sealed road") (mainly with either [chipseal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chipseal "Chipseal") or [asphalt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asphalt_concrete "Asphalt concrete")) for its entire length.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-4) From [Waitiki Landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waitiki_Landing "Waitiki Landing") south of Cape Reinga, SH 1 travels down the central-eastern side of the peninsula to [Kaitaia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaitaia "Kaitaia"), New Zealand's northernmost town, then travels through the [Mangamuka Gorge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mangamuka_Gorge "Mangamuka Gorge")[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-5) before turning south-east across the [Northland Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northland_Peninsula "Northland Peninsula") on to [Kawakawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawakawa,_New_Zealand "Kawakawa, New Zealand") in the [Bay of Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Islands "Bay of Islands") where the roadway is shared by the [Bay of Islands Vintage Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Islands_Vintage_Railway "Bay of Islands Vintage Railway") track, and then south to the city of [Whangārei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whang%C4%81rei "Whangārei"), the largest urban area in Northland.

SH 1 then skirts the south-western Whangārei Harbour, nearing the coast briefly at [Ruakākā](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruak%C4%81k%C4%81 "Ruakākā"), before proceeding down to wind through the [Brynderwyn Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brynderwyn_Hills "Brynderwyn Hills") before approaching the upper reaches of the [Kaipara Harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaipara_Harbour "Kaipara Harbour"). The highway crosses into the [Auckland Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland_Region "Auckland Region"), passing through [Wellsford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellsford "Wellsford").

Just north of [Warkworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warkworth,_New_Zealand "Warkworth, New Zealand"), SH 1 becomes the northernmost section of the [Auckland Northern Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland_Northern_Motorway "Auckland Northern Motorway"). This section was opened in 2023 and extends 18.5 km (11.5 mi) to the Johnstones Hill Tunnels, just south of [Puhoi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puhoi,_New_Zealand "Puhoi, New Zealand"). At this point the motorway becomes the Northern Gateway Toll Road, a 7.5 km (4.7 mi) section of automated [toll road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toll_road "Toll road") passing the [Hibiscus Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hibiscus_Coast "Hibiscus Coast") suburbs of [Orewa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orewa "Orewa") and [Silverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silverdale,_Auckland "Silverdale, Auckland"). From Silverdale, the motorway becomes toll-free, crossing farmland to [Albany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albany,_New_Zealand "Albany, New Zealand") and continuing past suburbs on the [North Shore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Shore_City "North Shore City") of [Auckland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland "Auckland"). The road crosses over the [Waitematā Harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waitemat%C4%81_Harbour "Waitematā Harbour") on the [Auckland Harbour Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland_Harbour_Bridge "Auckland Harbour Bridge") into Auckland's city centre and the [Central Motorway Junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Motorway_Junction "Central Motorway Junction"). At this junction, SH 1 becomes the [Auckland Southern Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland_Southern_Motorway "Auckland Southern Motorway"), and proceeds in a south-easterly direction across the [Auckland isthmus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland_isthmus "Auckland isthmus"), through [Manukau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manukau_City "Manukau City") and [Papakura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papakura "Papakura") to the top of the [Bombay Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay_Hills "Bombay Hills"), just short of the Auckland/[Waikato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikato "Waikato") boundary.

At Bombay, SH 1 becomes the [Waikato Expressway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikato_Expressway "Waikato Expressway"), a four-lane dual-carriageway expressway. The expressway takes the highway down the Bombay Hills to Mercer, where SH 1 meets the [Waikato River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikato_River "Waikato River"), which it broadly follows for the next 220 km (140 mi). The Waikato Expressway bypasses [Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamilton,_New_Zealand "Hamilton, New Zealand") city centre to the east, then bypasses [Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge,_New_Zealand "Cambridge, New Zealand") to the north before reverting to a single carriageway east of the town. The highway continues eastward to the town of [Tīrau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%C4%ABrau "Tīrau"), where it turns south to pass through [Putāruru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Put%C4%81ruru "Putāruru") and [Tokoroa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokoroa "Tokoroa") and the surrounding exotic [pine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pine "Pine") plantation forest area.

At Wairakei, SH 1 takes an eastern route to bypass [Taupō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taup%C5%8D "Taupō") and meet the [Lake Taupō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Taup%C5%8D "Lake Taupō") shoreline south of the town near [the airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taupo_Airport "Taupo Airport"). SH 1 follows the eastern shore of the lake for 50 km (31 mi) to [Tūrangi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%C5%ABrangi "Tūrangi"), at the southern end of the lake. Via SH32/41 the distance is about 6 km (3.7 mi) shorter than this section of SH1.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-6)

Turning southwards again, SH 1 leaves Tūrangi and ascends onto the [North Island Volcanic Plateau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Island_Volcanic_Plateau "North Island Volcanic Plateau"), passing through the fringes of the [Tongariro National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tongariro_National_Park "Tongariro National Park") and into the [Rangipo Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangipo_Desert "Rangipo Desert"), passing the volcanoes of [Ruapehu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Ruapehu "Mount Ruapehu"), [Ngauruhoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngauruhoe "Ngauruhoe") and [Tongariro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Tongariro "Mount Tongariro"). The road between Rangipo (10 km (6.2 mi) south of Tūrangi) and Waiouru is commonly known as the _Desert Road_. SH 1 enters the [Manawatū-Whanganui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manawat%C5%AB-Whanganui "Manawatū-Whanganui") Region, and descends through an army training area to the end of the Desert Road at [Waiouru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waiouru "Waiouru").

From Waiouru, the highway follows tributaries of the [Rangitikei River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangitikei_River "Rangitikei River") through [Taihape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taihape "Taihape") to meet the main river at Utiku. It then follows the western bank of the Rangitikei through [Ohingaiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohingaiti?action=edit&redlink=1 "Ohingaiti (page does not exist)") and [Hunterville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunterville "Hunterville") to [Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulls,_New_Zealand "Bulls, New Zealand"). At Bulls, SH 1 turns southeast to cross the river, turning southwest again 5 km (3.1 mi) down the road at [Sanson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanson,_New_Zealand "Sanson, New Zealand"). SH 1 crosses the [Manawatū Plains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manawat%C5%AB_Plains "Manawatū Plains"), passing the city of [Palmerston North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palmerston_North "Palmerston North") about 20 km (12 mi) west of it. It passes through [Foxton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foxton,_New_Zealand "Foxton, New Zealand"), before reaching the end of the plain at [Levin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levin,_New_Zealand "Levin, New Zealand").

From Levin, SH 1 follows the narrowing western coastal plain southwards. The highway crosses into the [Wellington Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellington_Region "Wellington Region")15 km (9 mi) south of Levin, and just north of [Ōtaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%8Ctaki,_New_Zealand "Ōtaki, New Zealand") widens into the [Kāpiti Expressway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C4%81piti_Expressway "Kāpiti Expressway"), a fully grade-separated four-lane dual carriageway. This expressway bypasses the Kāpiti conurbation of [Waikanae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikanae "Waikanae"), [Paraparaumu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraparaumu "Paraparaumu") and [Raumati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raumati_Beach "Raumati Beach"), before reaching the end of the coastal plain at [Mackays Crossing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mackays_Crossing "Mackays Crossing"). It then becomes the [Transmission Gully Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmission_Gully_Motorway "Transmission Gully Motorway") and steeply ascends through mountainous terrain to the Wainui Saddle, before descending through [its namesake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmission_Gully,_Wellington "Transmission Gully, Wellington") to [Pāuatahanui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P%C4%81uatahanui "Pāuatahanui") and bypassing [Porirua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porirua "Porirua") to the east before reaching the northern suburbs of [Wellington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellington "Wellington"), New Zealand's capital city.

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Ngahauranga_%28i.e._Ngauranga%29_Gorge_Road%2C_January_1912_ATLIB_337837.png/250px-Ngahauranga_%28i.e._Ngauranga%29_Gorge_Road%2C_January_1912_ATLIB_337837.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ngahauranga_(i.e._Ngauranga)_Gorge_Road,_January_1912_ATLIB_337837.png)

SH1 Ngauranga Gorge, 1912

Immediately after entering the city of [Wellington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellington "Wellington") in the suburb of [Linden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linden,_New_Zealand "Linden, New Zealand"), the Transmission Gully Motorway ends, and SH 1 merges on to the [Johnsonville-Porirua Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnsonville-Porirua_Motorway "Johnsonville-Porirua Motorway"). The motorway gradually ascends through [Tawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tawa,_New_Zealand "Tawa, New Zealand") before reaching [Johnsonville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnsonville,_New_Zealand "Johnsonville, New Zealand"). Here, the motorway ends, and SH 1 as a six-lane arterial road steeply descends through the [Ngauranga Gorge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngauranga_Gorge "Ngauranga Gorge") to the [Ngauranga Interchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngauranga_Interchange "Ngauranga Interchange"), on the shore of [Wellington Harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellington_Harbour "Wellington Harbour").

At [Ngauranga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngauranga "Ngauranga"), SH 1 becomes the [Wellington Urban Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellington_Urban_Motorway "Wellington Urban Motorway"), skirting the shore of the harbour then passing the city centre to the west. The motorway ends at [Te Aro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te_Aro "Te Aro"), where a one-way system takes traffic to the [Basin Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basin_Reserve "Basin Reserve"). Northbound traffic uses the [Wellington Inner City Bypass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellington_Inner_City_Bypass "Wellington Inner City Bypass") (opened 2007), while southbound traffic uses [Vivian Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Street "Vivian Street"). From the Basin Reserve, SH 1 travels through the [Mount Victoria Tunnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Victoria_Tunnel "Mount Victoria Tunnel") to Wellington's eastern suburbs and [Wellington International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellington_International_Airport "Wellington International Airport"). SH 1 ends at a roundabout at the entrance to the airport.

### South Island (SH 1S)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_Highway_1_(New_Zealand)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: South Island (SH 1S)")]

The South Island section of SH 1 starts in [Picton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picton,_New_Zealand "Picton, New Zealand"), adjacent to the railway station. Leaving Picton, SH 1 rises steeply to cross the Elevation saddle into the valley of the [Tuamarina River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuamarina_River "Tuamarina River"). It descends alongside this river and across the [Wairau Plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wairau_Plain?action=edit&redlink=1 "Wairau Plain (page does not exist)") before reaching Blenheim. SH 1 passes through Weld Pass and Dashwood Pass to enter the [Awatere Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Awatere_River "Awatere River"), then continues southward before passing [Lake Grassmere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Grassmere "Lake Grassmere"). From the small town of Ward the highway heads to the coast and follows it to [Kaikōura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaik%C5%8Dura "Kaikōura"). After passing Kaikōura, it veers inland, twisting through the [Hundalee Ranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hundalee_Ranges "Hundalee Ranges") before emerging at the northern end of the [Canterbury Plains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canterbury_Plains "Canterbury Plains").

The section of highway between the Clarence River and Hapuku Rivers north of Kaikōura was closed from 14 November 2016 to 15 December 2017, due to damage from the [2016 Kaikōura earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Kaik%C5%8Dura_earthquake "2016 Kaikōura earthquake").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-8)

SH 1 passes through [Amberley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amberley,_New_Zealand "Amberley, New Zealand") and [Woodend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodend,_New_Zealand "Woodend, New Zealand") before becoming the [Christchurch Northern Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christchurch_Northern_Motorway "Christchurch Northern Motorway") and bypassing [Kaiapoi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaiapoi "Kaiapoi") to the west. At The Groynes west of [Belfast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belfast,_New_Zealand "Belfast, New Zealand"), the motorway narrows to a four-lane divided arterial. SH 1 continues around the north-western urban fringe of [Christchurch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christchurch "Christchurch"), passing just east of [Christchurch International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christchurch_International_Airport "Christchurch International Airport"). At [Hornby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hornby,_New_Zealand "Hornby, New Zealand"), the highway turns south-west, narrows to a two-lane undivided road and passes through [Templeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Templeton,_New_Zealand "Templeton, New Zealand"). It then merges onto the [Christchurch Southern Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christchurch_Southern_Motorway "Christchurch Southern Motorway") where the highway becomes expressway standard until it approaches Rolleston.

South of Rolleston, SH 1 becomes virtually straight as it crosses the wide fan of the Canterbury plains, crossing the [country's longest road bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rakaia_Bridge "Rakaia Bridge") at [Rakaia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rakaia "Rakaia") before reaching [Ashburton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburton,_New_Zealand "Ashburton, New Zealand"), and then veering back towards the coast, which it reaches at Timaru. Between Ashburton and Timaru it crosses [Rangitata Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangitata_Island "Rangitata Island") in the [Rangitata River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangitata_River "Rangitata River").

South of Timaru, the road again passes through gentle hill country, staying close to the coast but largely out of sight of it. The road veers inland briefly, bypassing [Waimate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waimate "Waimate") as it reaches the plains around the mouth of the [Waitaki River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waitaki_River "Waitaki River"), which it crosses to enter [Otago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otago "Otago"). It passes through [Oamaru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oamaru "Oamaru"), from where it turns inland briefly, crossing undulating hill country before again reaching the coast at [Moeraki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moeraki "Moeraki"). From here the road again hugs the coast along [Katiki Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katiki_Beach "Katiki Beach"), remaining closer to the ocean than at any point since Kaikōura. The highway turns inland at Shag Point, passing through [Palmerston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palmerston,_New_Zealand "Palmerston, New Zealand") and [Waikouaiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikouaiti "Waikouaiti").

South of Waikouaiti the road again becomes steep, rising sharply over the [Kilmog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilmog "Kilmog") hill before dropping down to the coast at [Blueskin Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blueskin_Bay "Blueskin Bay"), then rising again via [Dunedin-Waitati Highway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunedin-Waitati_Highway "Dunedin-Waitati Highway") (a two- to four-lane [carriageway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carriageway "Carriageway") which used to be designated a [motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeway "Freeway")) to the northern outskirts of [Dunedin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunedin "Dunedin"). From here it descends a steep, twisting stretch of Pine Hill Road through [Pine Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pine_Hill,_New_Zealand "Pine Hill, New Zealand"), before passing the [University of Otago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Otago "University of Otago") and heading through the city centre. For much of its route through Central Dunedin the highway is split into two separate northbound and southbound roads, part of the city's [one-way street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-way_street "One-way street") system. These roads traverse the central city 2–3 blocks southeast of the heart of the [CBD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district"). At the southern end of central Dunedin, the highway becomes the [Caversham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caversham,_New_Zealand "Caversham, New Zealand") By-pass, which rises along the [Caversham Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caversham_Valley "Caversham Valley") before again becoming a motorway at the saddle of Lookout Point.

The four-lane motorway ([Dunedin Southern Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunedin_Southern_Motorway "Dunedin Southern Motorway")) runs through Dunedin's southern suburbs until the interchange with [SH 87](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Highway_87_(New_Zealand) "State Highway 87 (New Zealand)") at [Mosgiel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosgiel "Mosgiel"). SH 1 then heads southwest across the [Taieri Plains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taieri_Plains "Taieri Plains"). The area between the [Taieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taieri_River "Taieri River") and [Waipori Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waipori_River "Waipori River") is flood-prone, and the highway crosses this on a major embankment known colloquially as the _flood-free highway_. SH 1 continues through gentle hill country and along the shore of [Lake Waihola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Waihola "Lake Waihola"), then crosses the [Tokomairiro Plains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokomairiro_Plains "Tokomairiro Plains") into [Milton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton,_New_Zealand "Milton, New Zealand"). South of Milton is a major junction with [SH 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_8 "New Zealand State Highway 8") at Clarksville Junction. SH 1 continues to cross rolling hill country to reach [Balclutha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balclutha,_New_Zealand "Balclutha, New Zealand").

From Balclutha, the highway turns west, veering briefly north as it heads inland to avoid the rough hills of [The Catlins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Catlins "The Catlins"). It passes through the small town of [Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton,_New_Zealand "Clinton, New Zealand") before reaching the major provincial town of [Gore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gore,_New_Zealand "Gore, New Zealand"). Because of the names of these two towns, this stretch of the highway was christened "The Presidential Highway" during the time of the [Clinton-Gore administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Bill_Clinton "Presidency of Bill Clinton") in the United States. At Gore, the highway crosses the [Mataura River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mataura_River "Mataura River"); from here the road again turns south to roughly follow the river. The highway passes through [Mataura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mataura,_New_Zealand "Mataura, New Zealand") before turning west at [Edendale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edendale,_New_Zealand "Edendale, New Zealand"). Many travellers choose to turn onto [SH 93](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_93 "New Zealand State Highway 93") at Clinton, as this route shortens the journey between Clinton and Mataura by about 10 km (6.2 mi) and bypasses [Gore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gore,_New_Zealand "Gore, New Zealand").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-9) Over its last stretch the road veers southwest before reaching the city of [Invercargill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invercargill "Invercargill"). In central Invercargill it meets the southern end of [SH 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Highway_6_(New_Zealand) "State Highway 6 (New Zealand)") and turns due south, skirting the estuary of the [New River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_River,_New_Zealand "New River, New Zealand") and Bluff Harbour. It passes through the small town of [Bluff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluff,_New_Zealand "Bluff, New Zealand") before reaching its terminus at [Stirling Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stirling_Point "Stirling Point"), a kilometre south of Bluff. A commemorative signpost at Stirling Point indicates distances to major world centres and to the start of the highway at Picton.

SH 1 has two spurs, both in the vicinity of [Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamilton,_New_Zealand "Hamilton, New Zealand"):

*   **SH 1B** runs from SH 1N at [Taupiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taupiri "Taupiri") to SH 1N at [Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge,_New_Zealand "Cambridge, New Zealand"), and provides an eastern bypass of Hamilton. Gazetted in 1999, the 42 km (26 mi) highway utilises many roads which were previously under the administration of the [Waikato District Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikato_District_Council "Waikato District Council").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-10) Part of the highway also shares a concurrency with [SH 26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_26 "New Zealand State Highway 26"). Recent progress of construction of the [Waikato Expressway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikato_Expressway "Waikato Expressway") at Ngāruawāhia and Cambridge have also resulted in the curtailment of SH 1B at both the northern and southern termini.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-11) SH 1B is to be handed back to the Waikato District Council after the completion of the Hamilton section of the Waikato Expressway in 2022. Because it was not intended to be a permanent state highway, there are intersections where the state highway gives priority to local roads in several places.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-12)
*   **SH 1C** runs from SH 1N at [Horsham Downs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsham_Downs "Horsham Downs") to SH 1N at [Tamahere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamahere "Tamahere"). This was the former route of SH 1 through Hamilton, prior to the opening of the Hamilton section of the Waikato Expressway in July 2022. This route is 24 km (15 mi).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-SH_1C-13)

## Road conditions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_Highway_1_(New_Zealand)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Road conditions")]

SH 1 has varied road conditions. For most of its length it is a two-lane single carriageway road with at-grade intersections and access, sealed with chipseal in rural areas or asphalt in urban and high-traffic areas. The highway has frequent passing lanes on these sections, to allow traffic to pass other vehicles safely. Parts of the road are steep by international standards. Most steep sections having a combination of passing lanes (uphill), and crawler lanes or stopping bays (downhill) to allow heavy and slow vehicles to pull out of the way to let other vehicles pass.

[NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NZ_Transport_Agency_Waka_Kotahi "NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi") classifies the most part of State Highway 1 as a national strategic road. The exceptions are between [Kawakawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawakawa,_New_Zealand "Kawakawa, New Zealand") and [Whangārei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whang%C4%81rei "Whangārei") and south of Mosgiel, where the SH 1 is classified as a regional strategic road, and north of Kawakawa where SH 1 is classified as a primary collector road. The sections between [Wellsford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellsford "Wellsford") and [Wairakei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wairakei "Wairakei"), between [Ōhau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%8Chau "Ōhau") and [Wellington Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellington_International_Airport "Wellington International Airport"), and between [Woodend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodend,_New_Zealand "Woodend, New Zealand") and [Rolleston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolleston,_New_Zealand "Rolleston, New Zealand") are classified as high volume roads.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-15) The section from the Central Motorway Junction and the Newmarket Viaduct, 3 km (1.9 mi) to the south, is the country's busiest section of road, with more than 200,000 vehicle movements a day between [Khyber Pass Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khyber_Pass_Road,_New_Zealand "Khyber Pass Road, New Zealand") and Gillies Ave.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-NZTAFAQ-16)

[NZTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NZTA "NZTA") announced in September 2010 that it was replacing the last three [fords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_(crossing) "Ford (crossing)") on SH 1S. The shingle fan fords are near [Kaikōura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaik%C5%8Dura "Kaikōura"), and while generally being dry, on about 28 days a year state highway traffic used to detour around them due to high water levels on old single-lane bridges, leading to delays on a major freight route. With the detour bridges reaching the end of their lifespan, NZTA replaced the fords with [culverts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culvert "Culvert").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-17)

## Route changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_Highway_1_(New_Zealand)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Route changes")]

### Motorway and expressway upgrades

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_Highway_1_(New_Zealand)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Motorway and expressway upgrades")]

Construction of motorways and expressways has diverted the route of State Highway 1 in many places.

The opening of the [Auckland Harbour Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland_Harbour_Bridge "Auckland Harbour Bridge") and the [Auckland Northern Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland_Northern_Motorway "Auckland Northern Motorway") between Northcote Road and Fanshawe Street in May 1959 saw State Highway 1 diverted from its former route around the Waitematā Harbour. Northern extensions of the motorway in 1969 (to Tristram Avenue), 1979 (to Sunset Road) and 1984 (to Dairy Flat Highway via Greville Road) diverted State Highway 1 off Wairau Road and Albany Highway. A motorway extension from Greville Road to Silverdale in 1999 bypassed Dairy Flat Highway, which was re-designated State Highway 17. In 2009, the Northern Motorway was extended to Puhoi, bypassing Hibiscus Coast Highway through Orewa which was re-designated part of SH 17.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-AM2008-18) However, SH 17 was short lived, being revoked in September 2012 and reverting to a local arterial road.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-19) Ara Tuhono, the Puhoi to Warkworth motorway, was opened in June 2023.

The [Auckland Southern Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland_Southern_Motorway "Auckland Southern Motorway") was built between 1953 and 1978, bypassing the former route via [Great South Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_South_Road,_New_Zealand "Great South Road, New Zealand"). The construction of the [Central Motorway Junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Motorway_Junction "Central Motorway Junction") between 1973 and 1978 connected the Northern and Southern Motorways, taking State Highway 1 off inner Auckland streets.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-AM2008-18)

The [Waikato Expressway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikato_Expressway "Waikato Expressway") north of Te Kauwhata has largely been built on the existing line of SH 1N, although at [Pōkeno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P%C5%8Dkeno "Pōkeno") the highway was diverted to bypass the town to the east. South of Te Kauwhata, most of the expressway has been built on a new line bypassing the towns of [Ohinewai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohinewai "Ohinewai"), [Ngāruawāhia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C4%81ruaw%C4%81hia "Ngāruawāhia"), [Te Rapa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te_Rapa "Te Rapa") and [Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge,_New_Zealand "Cambridge, New Zealand"), as well as the city of [Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamilton,_New_Zealand "Hamilton, New Zealand"). Most old sections of SH 1N reverted to local arterial roads, while the former section through Hamilton became the SH 1C spur.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-SH_1C-13)

Construction of the Peka Peka to Ōtaki extension to the [Kāpiti Expressway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C4%81piti_Expressway "Kāpiti Expressway") began in mid 2017 and opened to traffic in December 2022.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-stuff-pp2o-open-20) The project added 13 kilometres (8 mi) of expressway to the northern end of the Kāpiti Expressway at Peka Peka, to terminate north of Ōtaki at Taylors Road.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-21)

The controversial [Transmission Gully Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmission_Gully_Motorway "Transmission Gully Motorway") began construction in 2014, and was officially opened on 30 March 2022.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-22) It provides a new alignment for State Highway 1 between [Mackays Crossing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mackays_Crossing "Mackays Crossing") and [Linden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linden,_New_Zealand "Linden, New Zealand"), diverting the route from the Centennial Highway between [Paekākāriki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paek%C4%81k%C4%81riki "Paekākāriki") and [Pukerua Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pukerua_Bay "Pukerua Bay"), as well as providing an eastern bypass of [Porirua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porirua "Porirua").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-Transmission_Gully_Gazette_notice-23) The previous route of State Highway 1 was renumbered to [State Highway 59](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Highway_59_(New_Zealand) "State Highway 59 (New Zealand)") on 7 December 2021, which created a temporary 26.2 kilometres (16.3 mi) gap in the SH 1 designation until the new motorway opened.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-SH_59_renumbering-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-State_Highway_59_switch_confirmed_for_December-25)

The [Johnsonville-Porirua Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnsonville-Porirua_Motorway "Johnsonville-Porirua Motorway") was constructed in the 1940s and 1950s to replace the [Old Porirua Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Porirua_Road "Old Porirua Road"). The first section of motorway between Johnsonville and Takapu Road opened on 23 December 1950, and is New Zealand's oldest motorway.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-27)

The [Wellington Urban Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellington_Urban_Motorway "Wellington Urban Motorway") was constructed between 1969 and 1978, but was originally part of State Highway 2 as it could only be accessed from the Hutt Valley. The construction of the Ngauranga Interchange flyovers in 1984 allowed SH 1 to be diverted onto the motorway, bypassing central Wellington streets.

The [Christchurch Northern Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christchurch_Northern_Motorway "Christchurch Northern Motorway") opened in October 1967 between Tram Road and Belfast, providing a second road crossing of the [Waimakariri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waimakariri_River "Waimakariri River").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-28) The motorway was extended northward to Pineacres in December 1970, bypassing [Kaiapoi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaiapoi "Kaiapoi").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-29) The [Western Belfast Bypass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Belfast_Bypass "Western Belfast Bypass") spur opened on 31 October 2017, extending the motorway southwest to The Groynes, allowing SH 1 traffic to bypass Belfast.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-30)

The extension of the [Dunedin Southern Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunedin_Southern_Motorway "Dunedin Southern Motorway") has also seen changes in the highway, notably to bypass the suburbs of [Fairfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairfield,_Otago "Fairfield, Otago") and Sunnyvale.

For the history of realignments between Mackays Crossing and Linden, see [State Highway 59 (New Zealand)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Highway_59_(New_Zealand) "State Highway 59 (New Zealand)") and [Transmission Gully Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmission_Gully_Motorway "Transmission Gully Motorway").

In Hamilton, SH 1N originally ran through the city centre via Te Rapa Road, Ulster Street (first agreed as an alternative to the northern end of Victoria St in 1930),[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-31) Victoria Street, Bridge Street and Cobham Drive; this original route later became Hamilton Urban Route 4. In 1992, SH 1N was diverted to run through [Frankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankton,_Hamilton "Frankton, Hamilton") via Avalon Drive, Greenwood Street, Kahikatea Drive and Normandy Avenue.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-32) The Frankton route then became the SH 1C spur in July 2022, with SH 1N being diverted to the newly opened Hamilton section of the [Waikato Expressway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikato_Expressway "Waikato Expressway").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-SH_1C-13)

In Christchurch, SH 1S originally ran via the city centre rather than around the outskirts via Harewood. The original route was via Main North Road, Cranford Street, Sherborne Street, Bealey Avenue, Madras and Gasson Streets (north)/Barbadoes Street and Waltham Road (south), Brougham Street, the Christchurch Southern Arterial Motorway, Curletts Road, Blenheim Road, and Main South Road.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-33) The section from the Queen Elizabeth II Drive to Brougham Street is now a local road, while the remainder of the route forms parts of SH 74 and 76.

Re-routing also occurred in Whangarei in 1979, and Timaru, removing SH 1 from their city centres. The original route through Whangārei via Kamo Road, Bank Street, Water Street and Maunu Road was diverted via Western Hills Drive, which was built from 1977 to 1979, while the original route through Timaru via Stafford and King Streets was diverted via Theodosia Street and Craigie Avenue.

In 2010, the Taupō Bypass was constructed shifting the original SH 1 from the township and lakeside to the eastern outskirts of Taupō. The bypass starts at Wairakei near the existing SH 1/SH 5 intersection and finishes to the north of Taupo Airport. The concurrency with SH 5 also follows part of the bypass.

In the southern South Island, several particularly twisting sections of SH 1S have been rebuilt to remove sharp bends and to generally improve road conditions. These include stretches at Normanby, near Timaru; [Waianakarua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waianakarua "Waianakarua"); two stretches at Flag Swamp and [Tumai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumai "Tumai") between [Palmerston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palmerston,_New_Zealand "Palmerston, New Zealand") and [Waikouaiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikouaiti "Waikouaiti");[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-35) and on the [Dunedin Northern Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunedin_Northern_Motorway "Dunedin Northern Motorway") near [Waitati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waitati "Waitati").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-37) An extensive section between [Allanton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allanton,_New_Zealand "Allanton, New Zealand") and the [Taieri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taieri_River "Taieri River") was realigned during the 1970s.

### Former spurs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_Highway_1_(New_Zealand)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Former spurs")]

**SH 1A** ran from [Orewa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orewa "Orewa") to [Silverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silverdale,_Auckland "Silverdale, Auckland"). When the [Northern Gateway Toll Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland_Northern_Motorway "Auckland Northern Motorway") opened, part of SH 1A was incorporated into SH 1N and the rest had its highway status revoked.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-38)

**SH 1F** was the name previously given to the northernmost section of SH 1N – between Cape Reinga and the junction with [SH 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_10 "New Zealand State Highway 10"). This section is no longer a spur and is now part of SH 1N.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-39)

Where SH 1 has moved onto a bypass, sometimes the former route is designated a spur until such time as the road can be transferred to the local council. All these routes are unsigned and appear as local arterial roads on maps.

*   **SH 1D** was assigned to the former SH 1S route between [Abbotsford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbotsford,_New_Zealand "Abbotsford, New Zealand") and Saddle Hill in southern [Dunedin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunedin "Dunedin"), via the suburbs of [Sunnyvale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunnyvale,_Otago "Sunnyvale, Otago") and [Fairfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairfield,_Otago "Fairfield, Otago"). The route was the bypassed Fairfield section of the [Dunedin Southern Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunedin_Southern_Motorway "Dunedin Southern Motorway") in 2003.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
*   **SH 1G** was assigned to the former SH 1N route between Taupiri and Horotiu via Ngāruawāhia. This section was bypassed by [Waikato Expressway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikato_Expressway "Waikato Expressway") in December 2013.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
*   **SH 1H** was assigned to the former SH 1N route through [Huntly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntly "Huntly") and [Taupiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taupiri "Taupiri"). This section was bypassed by [Waikato Expressway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikato_Expressway "Waikato Expressway") in December 2022.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-40)
*   **SH 1J** was assigned to the former SH 1S route through [Belfast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belfast,_New_Zealand "Belfast, New Zealand"). This section was bypassed by the [Western Belfast Bypass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Belfast_Bypass "Western Belfast Bypass") in December 2017.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-41)
*   **SH 1K** was assigned to the former SH 1N route between Raumati and Peka Peka via Paraparaumu and Waikanae. This section was bypassed by [Kāpiti Expressway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C4%81piti_Expressway "Kāpiti Expressway") in March 2017.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-42)
*   **SH 1P** was assigned to the former SH 1N route between [Peka Peka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peka_Peka "Peka Peka") and [Ōtaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%8Ctaki,_New_Zealand "Ōtaki, New Zealand") via [Te Horo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te_Horo "Te Horo"). This section was bypassed by [Kāpiti Expressway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C4%81piti_Expressway "Kāpiti Expressway") in December 2022.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-43)
*   **SH 1T** was assigned to the [Transmission Gully Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmission_Gully_Motorway "Transmission Gully Motorway") during construction, before the SH 1 designation was formally altered. It was revoked before the Transmission Gully Motorway opened in March 2022.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-44)

## Future improvements

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_Highway_1_(New_Zealand)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Future improvements")]

State Highway 1 has been earmarked for several motorway projects most of which have surfaced from the National government's [Roads of National Significance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roads_of_National_Significance "Roads of National Significance") package announced in 2009.

### Northland

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_Highway_1_(New_Zealand)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Northland")]

The section of [Marsden Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marsden_Point "Marsden Point") to [Whangārei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whang%C4%81rei "Whangārei") will be upgraded to a four lane expressway as part of the [Roads of National Significance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roads_of_National_Significance "Roads of National Significance") programme.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-45)

### Auckland

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_Highway_1_(New_Zealand)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Auckland")]

The [Puhoi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puhoi,_New_Zealand "Puhoi, New Zealand") to [Wellsford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellsford "Wellsford") motorway (Ara Tūhono) is one of the projects of the [Roads of National Significance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roads_of_National_Significance "Roads of National Significance").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-46) Construction of the 18.5 km (11.5 mi) Puhoi to Warkworth section began on 8 December 2016 with the official sod-turning. The motorway runs west of the current SH 1 alignment, starting at the end of the existing Auckland Northern Motorway and terminating onto the existing highway at Kaipara Flats Road, north of Warkworth township. The new motorway opened in June 2023.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-47) The NZTA released its preferred alignment for the Warkworth to Wellsford section for consultation in February 2017. The motorway will run from the Puhoi to Warkworth section west of Warkworth northward, passing east of Wellsford and Te Hana to terminate onto the existing highway at Mangawhai Road, just short of the Auckland/Northland boundary.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-48)

Many ideas have come forth to create a [Second Harbour Crossing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Harbour_Crossing,_Auckland "Second Harbour Crossing, Auckland") over Waitematā Harbour to complement the aging Auckland Harbour Bridge.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-49) These include ideas for a second bridge, or a second tunnel with capacity for rail. At this stage, any meaningful progress is unlikely until at least 2025.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-50)

### Waikato Expressway

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_Highway_1_(New_Zealand)&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Waikato Expressway")]

As of October 2017, the NZTA is investigating extending the Waikato Expressway south of Cambridge 16 km (9.9 mi) to the SH 1/SH 29 intersection at Piarere, bypassing the existing highway around the shores of [Lake Karapiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Karapiro "Lake Karapiro").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-51)

### Levin to Wellington Airport

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_Highway_1_(New_Zealand)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Levin to Wellington Airport")]

In February 2018, NZTA began investigation into extending the Kāpiti Expressway further northward approximately 23 km (14 mi) to just north of [Levin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levin,_New_Zealand "Levin, New Zealand"), bypassing Levin and the villages of Ohau and [Manakau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manakau "Manakau").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-53) In December 2018, the NZTA selected the road's preferred corridor, bypassing Levin to the east alongside part of SH 57.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-54) Funding was approved by the government in January 2020.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-Newshub:transport-55)

Many inner city Wellington projects are also planned for SH 1 including duplication of the Terrace Tunnel and Mt Victoria tunnels. However these projects look uncertain as another planned project, the Basin Reserve Flyover failed to obtain the necessary resource consents and an appeal was rejected in the [High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Court_of_New_Zealand "High Court of New Zealand").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-56)

### Canterbury

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_Highway_1_(New_Zealand)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Canterbury")]

NZTA are to extend the [Christchurch Northern Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christchurch_Northern_Motorway "Christchurch Northern Motorway") so that it bypasses the town of [Woodend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodend,_New_Zealand "Woodend, New Zealand") to terminate at [Pegasus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pegasus,_New_Zealand "Pegasus, New Zealand").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-57)

### Other improvements

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_Highway_1_(New_Zealand)&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Other improvements")]

Several smaller projects are being undertaken to improve sections of SH 1. These include:

*   Widening the Southern Motorway between Papakura and Drury South from four to six lanes.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-Stuff:announcement-58) In June 2021 it was announced that funding for this project would be indefinitely deferred.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-59)
*   Widening the Waimakariri River bridges on the Christchurch Northern Motorway from four to six lanes.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-60)
*   Raising the highway and installing culverts in flood-prone areas between Oamaru and the Kakanui River bridge.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-61)

**State Highway 1** (**SH 1**) is the longest and most significant road in the [New Zealand road network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_state_highway_network "New Zealand state highway network"), running the length of both main islands. It appears on road maps as SH 1 and on road signs as a white number 1 on a red shield, but it has the official designations SH 1N in the [North Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Island "North Island") and SH 1S in the [South Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Island "South Island").

SH 1 is 2,006 kilometres (1,246 mi) long, 1,074 km (667 mi) in the North Island[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-1) and 932 km (579 mi) in the South Island.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-2) Since 2010 new roads have reduced the length from 2,033 km (1,263 mi).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-3) For the majority of its length it is a two-lane [single carriageway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_carriageway "Single carriageway"), with [at-grade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/At-grade_intersection "At-grade intersection") intersections and property accesses, in both rural and urban areas. These sections have some passing lanes. Around 315 km (196 mi) of SH 1 is of motorway or expressway standard as of August 2022[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_Highway_1_(New_Zealand)&action=edit): 281 km (175 mi) in the North Island and 34 km (21 mi) in the South Island.[_[needs update](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers#Chronological\_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_]

### North Island (SH 1N)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_Highway_1_(New_Zealand)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: North Island (SH 1N)")]

SH 1 starts at [Cape Reinga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Reinga "Cape Reinga"), at the northwestern tip of the [Aupōuri Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aup%C5%8Duri_Peninsula "Aupōuri Peninsula"), and since April 2010 has been [sealed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sealed_road "Sealed road") (mainly with either [chipseal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chipseal "Chipseal") or [asphalt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asphalt_concrete "Asphalt concrete")) for its entire length.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-4) From [Waitiki Landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waitiki_Landing "Waitiki Landing") south of Cape Reinga, SH 1 travels down the central-eastern side of the peninsula to [Kaitaia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaitaia "Kaitaia"), New Zealand's northernmost town, then travels through the [Mangamuka Gorge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mangamuka_Gorge "Mangamuka Gorge")[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-5) before turning south-east across the [Northland Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northland_Peninsula "Northland Peninsula") on to [Kawakawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawakawa,_New_Zealand "Kawakawa, New Zealand") in the [Bay of Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Islands "Bay of Islands") where the roadway is shared by the [Bay of Islands Vintage Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Islands_Vintage_Railway "Bay of Islands Vintage Railway") track, and then south to the city of [Whangārei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whang%C4%81rei "Whangārei"), the largest urban area in Northland.

SH 1 then skirts the south-western Whangārei Harbour, nearing the coast briefly at [Ruakākā](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruak%C4%81k%C4%81 "Ruakākā"), before proceeding down to wind through the [Brynderwyn Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brynderwyn_Hills "Brynderwyn Hills") before approaching the upper reaches of the [Kaipara Harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaipara_Harbour "Kaipara Harbour"). The highway crosses into the [Auckland Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland_Region "Auckland Region"), passing through [Wellsford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellsford "Wellsford").

Just north of [Warkworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warkworth,_New_Zealand "Warkworth, New Zealand"), SH 1 becomes the northernmost section of the [Auckland Northern Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland_Northern_Motorway "Auckland Northern Motorway"). This section was opened in 2023 and extends 18.5 km (11.5 mi) to the Johnstones Hill Tunnels, just south of [Puhoi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puhoi,_New_Zealand "Puhoi, New Zealand"). At this point the motorway becomes the Northern Gateway Toll Road, a 7.5 km (4.7 mi) section of automated [toll road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toll_road "Toll road") passing the [Hibiscus Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hibiscus_Coast "Hibiscus Coast") suburbs of [Orewa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orewa "Orewa") and [Silverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silverdale,_Auckland "Silverdale, Auckland"). From Silverdale, the motorway becomes toll-free, crossing farmland to [Albany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albany,_New_Zealand "Albany, New Zealand") and continuing past suburbs on the [North Shore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Shore_City "North Shore City") of [Auckland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland "Auckland"). The road crosses over the [Waitematā Harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waitemat%C4%81_Harbour "Waitematā Harbour") on the [Auckland Harbour Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland_Harbour_Bridge "Auckland Harbour Bridge") into Auckland's city centre and the [Central Motorway Junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Motorway_Junction "Central Motorway Junction"). At this junction, SH 1 becomes the [Auckland Southern Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland_Southern_Motorway "Auckland Southern Motorway"), and proceeds in a south-easterly direction across the [Auckland isthmus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland_isthmus "Auckland isthmus"), through [Manukau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manukau_City "Manukau City") and [Papakura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papakura "Papakura") to the top of the [Bombay Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay_Hills "Bombay Hills"), just short of the Auckland/[Waikato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikato "Waikato") boundary.

At Bombay, SH 1 becomes the [Waikato Expressway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikato_Expressway "Waikato Expressway"), a four-lane dual-carriageway expressway. The expressway takes the highway down the Bombay Hills to Mercer, where SH 1 meets the [Waikato River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikato_River "Waikato River"), which it broadly follows for the next 220 km (140 mi). The Waikato Expressway bypasses [Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamilton,_New_Zealand "Hamilton, New Zealand") city centre to the east, then bypasses [Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge,_New_Zealand "Cambridge, New Zealand") to the north before reverting to a single carriageway east of the town. The highway continues eastward to the town of [Tīrau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%C4%ABrau "Tīrau"), where it turns south to pass through [Putāruru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Put%C4%81ruru "Putāruru") and [Tokoroa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokoroa "Tokoroa") and the surrounding exotic [pine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pine "Pine") plantation forest area.

At Wairakei, SH 1 takes an eastern route to bypass [Taupō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taup%C5%8D "Taupō") and meet the [Lake Taupō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Taup%C5%8D "Lake Taupō") shoreline south of the town near [the airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taupo_Airport "Taupo Airport"). SH 1 follows the eastern shore of the lake for 50 km (31 mi) to [Tūrangi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%C5%ABrangi "Tūrangi"), at the southern end of the lake. Via SH32/41 the distance is about 6 km (3.7 mi) shorter than this section of SH1.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_State_Highway_1#cite_note-6)

Turning southwards again, SH 1 leaves Tūrangi and ascends onto the [North Island Volcanic Plateau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Island_Volcanic_Plateau "North Island Volcanic Plateau"), passing through the fringes of the [Tongariro National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tongariro_National_Park "Tongariro National Park") and into the [Rangipo Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangipo_Desert "Rangipo Desert"), passing the volcanoes of [Ruapehu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Ruapehu "Mount Ruapehu"), [Ngauruhoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngauruhoe "Ngauruhoe") and [Tongariro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Tongariro "Mount Tongariro"). The road between Rangipo (10 km (6.2 mi) south of Tūrangi) and Waiouru is commonly known as the _Desert Road_. SH 1 enters the [Manawatū-Whanganui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manawat%C5%AB-Whanganui "Manawatū-Whanganui") Region, and descends through an army training area to the end of the Desert Road at [Waiouru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waiouru "Waiouru").

From Waiouru, the highway follows tributaries of the [Rangitikei River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangitikei_River "Rangitikei River") through [Taihape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taihape "Taihape") to meet the main river at Utiku. It then follows the western bank of the Rangitikei through [Ohingaiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohingaiti?action=edit&redlink=1 "Ohingaiti (page does not exist)") and [Hunterville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunterville "Hunterville") to [Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulls,_New_Zealand "Bulls, New Zealand"). At Bulls, SH 1 turns southeast to cross the river, turning southwest again 5 km (3.1 mi) down the road at [Sanson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanson,_New_Zealand "Sanson, New Zealand"). SH 1 crosses the [Manawatū Plains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manawat%C5%AB_Plains "Manawatū Plains"), passing the city of [Palmerston North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palmerston_North "Palmerston North") about 20 km (12 mi) west of it. It passes through [Foxton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foxton,_New_Zealand "Foxton, New Zealand"), before reaching the end of the plain at [Levin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levin,_New_Zealand "Levin, New Zealand").

From Levin, SH 1 follows the narrowing western coastal plain southwards. The highway crosses into the [Wellington Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellington_Region "Wellington Region")15 km (9 mi) south of Levin, and just north of [Ōtaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%8Ctaki,_New_Zealand "Ōtaki, New Zealand") widens into the [Kāpiti Expressway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C4%81piti_Expressway "Kāpiti Expressway"), a fully grade-separated four-lane dual carriageway. This expressway bypasses the Kāpiti conurbation of [Waikanae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikanae "Waikanae"), [Paraparaumu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraparaumu "Paraparaumu") and [Raumati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raumati_Beach "Raumati Beach"), before reaching the end of the coastal plain at [Mackays Crossing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mackays_Crossing "Mackays Crossing"). It then becomes the [Transmission Gully Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmission_Gully_Motorway "Transmission Gully Motorway") and steeply ascends through mountainous terrain to the Wainui Saddle, before descending through [its namesake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmission_Gully,_Wellington "Transmission Gully, Wellington") to [Pāuatahanui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P%C4%81uatahanui "Pāuatahanui") and bypassing [Porirua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porirua "Porirua") to the east before reaching the northern suburbs of [Wellington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellington "Wellington"), New Zealand's capital city.
